resources.string: Bulle sits around the camera and changes shape with what’s happening: a discreet pill, a compact view, then a full card with a single gesture.
A timer and your music? The bubble splits in two so everything stays in sight.
Tap, swipe, hold: every gesture triggers the action you choose. And everything stays on your phone.
The island is waiting around your camera. You can review every permission in Bulle’s settings.
Essential permissions still missing: %1$d. You can come back to them later.
Unlocks accessibility and notification access for an app installed outside the Play Store.
Android blocks some sensitive settings for apps installed outside the Play Store. Unlock them once before going on.
Open Bulle’s app info with the button below.
Tap the ⋮ menu at the top right, then “Allow restricted settings” and confirm.
No ⋮ menu? First try to enable Bulle in accessibility (next step): the option appears after the “Restricted setting” message.
Draws the island over other apps and runs your gestures.
This is the heart of Bulle: it draws the island around the camera and runs the gestures you choose. Bulle never reads your screen content.
In the list, tap “Bulle” (sometimes under “Installed apps” or “Downloaded services”), then turn it on.
Music, timers, calls and live updates in the island.
Bulle reads notifications to show music, timers, calls and live updates. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
The discreet notification that keeps the island alive.
Bulle shows a discreet notification so the system doesn’t stop it, and tells you when an update is ready.
Install Bulle updates from within the app.
Bulle isn’t on the Play Store: this permission lets it install its own updates in one tap.
Stops the system from putting the island to sleep.
Without this exemption, the system puts Bulle to sleep and the island disappears after a few minutes. The impact on battery life is negligible.
Essential on Honor: MagicOS kills background apps very aggressively.
Allow Bulle to start and stay active in the background.
MagicOS decides on its own which apps may run and eventually stops Bulle. Switch it to manual management:
Open “App launch” with the button below.
Find Bulle and turn off “Manage automatically”.
In the dialog, turn on “Auto-launch”, “Secondary launch” and “Run in background”.
Your phone may stop apps in the background. If the island disappears, allow Bulle to auto-start in the manufacturer’s settings. This step is optional.
Battery of earbuds and connected devices.
Brightness and rotation from the Deck.
Lets Bulle restart its service if the system stops it. Granted from a computer.
Only requested when you turn on the related feature.
The accessibility service is connected. All good.
Bulle is checked in accessibility, but the system stopped the service. Turn Bulle off and on again, or use automatic re-enable.
Bulle isn’t checked in accessibility. The system may have removed it after an update or a reboot.
Re-enable refused: grant the permission via adb first.
With this special permission, Bulle turns its accessibility service back on by itself when the system stops it. It is granted once, from a computer: enable USB debugging, plug in the phone, then run:
The permission stays valid until Bulle is uninstalled.
